title: Minimum Wage in Sydney: Your Guide to Annual, Fortnightly, and Tax Estimates
description: Learn how to convert the minimum wage in Sydney to annual pay, fortnightly earnings, and after-tax income. Includes 2026-27 tax rates, super, and casual loading.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is about $52,277, with super and tax estimated on top.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage in Sydney for 2026-27?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage applies across Australia, including Sydney. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Some awards or enterprise agreements may set higher rates for specific industries.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the minimum wage of $26.44, annual gross pay is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,277.44. Use the timesheet on this site to enter your own rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and after-tax figures.

faqs.q: Does the minimum wage include casual loading?
faqs.a: No. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour is the base rate for permanent employees. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making it $33.05 per hour. When using the timesheet, enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box to add 25% automatically.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Basics

Converting your hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. For most full-time roles, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This article uses that assumption unless stated otherwise. Knowing your annual figure helps you compare job offers, plan your budget, and estimate tax and super.

A fortnightly figure is also useful for pay cycles. Simply multiply your weekly earnings by two. For example, at the National Minimum Wage, weekly pay is $1,004.90, so fortnightly pay is $2,009.80 before tax.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Many industries have award rates that are higher, so check your specific award via the [pay guides](/blog) on this site.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. That makes the casual minimum wage $33.05 per hour. When using the [timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% automatically.

## Minimum Wage in Sydney: What It Means for Your Pay

Sydney, like all Australian cities, follows the National Minimum Wage. However, some Sydney-specific awards (such as hospitality or retail) may set higher rates. If you are covered by an award, your minimum pay could be above $26.44 per hour. The [reference tables](/data) on this site list common award rates. Remember, the National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a median. For a broader view of earnings, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time average weekly earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026. That is an average across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job.

## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

Let’s walk through the calculation using the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week:

- **Weekly**: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (close to the official $1,004.90 due to rounding)
- **Fortnightly**: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- **Annual**: $1,004.72 × 52 = $52,245.44 (the official figure is $52,277.44 using $1,004.90 × 52)

For a higher rate, say the average full-time ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, annual pay would be $2,083.70 × 52 = $108,352.40. That is an average, not a median for your job. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see your own figures.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Salary

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates from the Australian Taxation Office:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For the minimum wage annual salary of $52,277.44, the tax estimate is:

- Tax on $18,200: $0
- Tax on $26,800 (from $18,201 to $45,000): $4,020
- Tax on $7,277.44 (from $45,001 to $52,277.44): $2,183.23
- Total tax: $6,203.23
- Medicare (2%): $1,045.55
- Total deductions: $7,248.78
- After-tax annual income: approximately $45,028.66

Note: Medicare reduction thresholds for 2026–27 were not confirmed at the time of this estimate, so the 2025–26 single thresholds are used. This is an estimate only. For a personalised calculation, see the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For the minimum wage example:

- Annual ordinary earnings: $52,277.44
- Super (12%): $6,273.29
- Total employment cost: $58,550.73

The super guarantee has a maximum contribution base of $270,830 for 2026–27, so this cap does not affect minimum wage earners. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is additional. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

The [timesheet](/), which is the home page of this site, lets you enter your base hourly rate and instantly see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top of the base rate—never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. You can also explore [pay guides](/blog) for award rates, [reference tables](/data) for averages, and [job pay](/topics/job-pay) for industry-specific information.

## Important Considerations

This article provides estimates based on a 38-hour week and 52-week year. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a precise calculation tailored to your situation, consult the Fair Work Ombudsman for pay rates and the Australian Taxation Office for tax obligations.
